title: Where Does ChatGPT Get Its Information? (Explained)
excerpt: ChatGPT uses training data, live web search and your own context. See its sources, which OpenAI bots crawl sites, and how brands become a cited source.
keywords: where does ChatGPT get its information
where does ChatGPT get its info from
how does ChatGPT get its information
does ChatGPT get information from the internet
author: AI Brand Track Team
content:
ChatGPT gets its information from two places: what its underlying model learned during training, and what it looks up at the moment you ask. Training data comes from publicly available web content, data licensed from third parties, and material provided or generated by users, human trainers and researchers. On top of that, ChatGPT can search the web live, and it can draw on your own context: memory, custom instructions, files you upload and apps you connect.

Knowing which source shaped an answer tells you how much to trust it, and, if you run a business, how to influence what ChatGPT says about you. This guide walks through each source using OpenAI's own documentation. If you want the practical tracking workflow instead, see our guide on [how to track brand mentions in ChatGPT](/blog/how-to-track-chatgpt-brand-mentions).

## Source 1: Training data (what the model already knows)

OpenAI's help article on [how ChatGPT and its foundation models are developed](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed) describes three primary sources of information:

1. **Information that is publicly available on the internet**, such as public web pages, forums, blogs and posts.
2. **Information OpenAI partners with third parties to access**, for example datasets licensed under agreements.
3. **Information that users, human trainers and researchers provide or generate.**

OpenAI also says it increasingly uses **synthetic data**, meaning training material generated with the help of its own models, for things like extra multilingual examples or to fill gaps where real data is sparse.

A few details from OpenAI's description are worth knowing:

- **Only freely accessible content.** OpenAI says it does not intentionally collect data from sources known to be behind paywalls or from the dark web.
- **Filtering.** Material such as hate speech, adult content, sites that aggregate personal information and spam is filtered out before training.
- **Website owners can opt out.** Blocking OpenAI's training crawler, GPTBot, in robots.txt signals that a site's content should not be used to train its foundation models.
- **No stored copies.** According to OpenAI, the model does not keep copies of the documents it was trained on. Training adjusts the model's internal parameters (its "weights") to reflect patterns, and the model then predicts new text one token at a time.

That last point explains a lot about how ChatGPT behaves. It is not looking your answer up in a database of saved pages. It is generating the most plausible continuation based on patterns, which is why it can sound fluent and still be wrong.

### The knowledge cutoff

Every model is trained on data up to a certain point. In its help article [Does ChatGPT tell the truth?](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8313428-does-chatgpt-tell-the-truth), OpenAI states plainly that responses do not incorporate information about events after that cutoff unless tools such as search are used. Cutoffs differ between models, and newer models generally have later cutoffs, so the exact date depends on which model answered.

For brands, this means a rebrand, new pricing or product launch that happened after the cutoff will not show up in answers that rely on training data alone. Those answers only catch up when a newer model is trained and released.

## Source 2: Live web search

ChatGPT can search the web to answer questions with current information and links to sources. According to OpenAI's help article on [searching the web with ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt):

- ChatGPT **may search automatically** when a question would benefit from current information, and users can also start a search manually from the tools menu.
- Web search is available on Free and paid plans, and **people who are not signed in can use it too.**
- Search-enabled answers can include **inline citations** and a **Sources** panel listing cited pages and other relevant links.

### How a search actually runs

OpenAI explains that ChatGPT search sometimes partners with other search providers. When it does, ChatGPT typically **rewrites your question into one or more targeted search queries** and sends those to the provider, then may send follow-up queries after reviewing the first results. OpenAI's help page links to the privacy policies of Microsoft and Shopify as search-related partners.

Two other inputs shape the search:

- **Approximate location.** ChatGPT collects general location from your IP address and may include it in rewritten queries (for example turning "restaurants near me" into a city-specific search). It says it does not share your IP address or account details with search providers.
- **Memory.** If memory is enabled, ChatGPT may use relevant saved memories when rewriting a search query.

So the same question can trigger different searches for different people, which is one reason answers vary. We cover that in detail in [does ChatGPT give the same answer to everyone?](/blog/does-chatgpt-give-the-same-answer-to-everyone)

### Does ChatGPT get its information from Google?

OpenAI does not say that ChatGPT uses Google. Its help page says ChatGPT search "sometimes partners with other search providers" and points to Microsoft's and Shopify's privacy statements. OpenAI also runs its own crawler, OAI-SearchBot, to surface websites in ChatGPT search. Beyond that, OpenAI does not publish a full list of where search results come from.

### What about ads in ChatGPT?

OpenAI started testing ads in the United States on February 9, 2026, for users on the Free and Go plans; paid plans such as Plus and Pro do not show ads. According to OpenAI's [ads help article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001047-ads-in-chatgpt), ads appear below a response, are clearly labeled, run on systems separate from the chat model and do not influence ChatGPT's answers. Ads are therefore not an information source for the answer itself, and paying for ads does not buy a mention in it.

## Which OpenAI bots visit websites

OpenAI documents several user agents on its [crawlers and user agents page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots). Each one does a different job, and each is controlled separately in robots.txt.

| User agent | What it does | Does robots.txt apply? | What blocking it means |
|---|---|---|---|
| **OAI-SearchBot** | Surfaces websites in ChatGPT's search features | Yes | Your pages won't be shown in ChatGPT search answers, though they can still appear as navigational links. OpenAI says changes take about 24 hours to take effect. |
| **ChatGPT-User** | Visits a page when a user's request requires it (including Custom GPT actions) | May not apply, because the visit is user-initiated | Not used to decide what appears in search, and not used for automatic crawling |
| **GPTBot** | Crawls content that may be used to train OpenAI's foundation models | Yes | Signals your content should not be used for training |
| **OAI-AdsBot** | Checks landing pages submitted as ads in ChatGPT | Not stated | Only visits submitted ad pages; OpenAI says its data is not used for training |

The settings are independent. You can allow OAI-SearchBot (to be eligible for ChatGPT search) while disallowing GPTBot (to opt out of training). OpenAI notes that if you allow both, it may use a single crawl for both purposes.

## Source 3: Your own context

The third source is you. OpenAI's [memory documentation](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-in-chatgpt) lists the personal context ChatGPT may draw on, depending on plan and region:

- **Past chats** (when chat history referencing is on)
- **Saved memories**
- **Custom instructions**, which OpenAI says take effect immediately once you update them
- **Files in your Library** and files uploaded to a conversation
- **Content from connected apps**, such as Gmail or Google Drive

When personal context shapes an answer, a Sources section may show which past chat, memory, file or email contributed, though OpenAI notes this may not show every factor. This also answers a popular question, "How does ChatGPT know so much about me?" Usually it is because you told it, in earlier chats, memories, instructions or connected accounts.

## How the sources compare

| Source | How fresh | Shows sources? | Same for everyone? | What a brand can influence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Training data | Fixed at the model's cutoff | No | Mostly, for the same model | Long-term public footprint: your site, reviews, coverage, forums |
| Live web search | Current | Usually, via citations | No: query rewriting, location and memory vary | Crawlability, page clarity, presence on the pages that get cited |
| Personal context | Whatever the user shared | Sometimes | No, unique per user | Very little directly |

## Citations: which sites get cited, and are they real?

In search-enabled answers, citations point to real pages that ChatGPT retrieved. OpenAI's own guidance, though, is that search results and citations can be incomplete, outdated or incorrect, and it recommends opening the cited source to confirm it actually supports the claim.

Answers *without* search are a different story. OpenAI's help article on accuracy lists fabricated quotes, studies, citations and references to non-existent sources as a known form of hallucination. If ChatGPT gives you a reference without a clickable citation from a search, treat it as unverified.

OpenAI does not publish a list of which kinds of sites it prefers to cite. In practice, the citations you see for commercial questions often include comparison and "best of" articles, review platforms, directories, community forums, official documentation and the brands' own sites. Rather than guessing, open the Sources panel for the questions your buyers ask and note which domains come up repeatedly. Those are the pages that shape ChatGPT's view of your category.

## Accuracy limits you should expect

OpenAI's documentation names several limitations directly:

- **Hallucinations:** incorrect facts, dates or definitions, and invented references.
- **Confidence isn't reliability:** the model can sound sure while being wrong.
- **Lack of access:** it may not reach a page because of technical issues, paywalls or robots.txt preferences.
- **Bias and oversimplification:** presenting one perspective as settled, or flattening nuanced topics.

For high-stakes topics (medical, legal, financial), use search with citations, open the sources and check them against an authoritative reference.

## What this means for brands: how to become a source

Because ChatGPT pulls from training data and live search, there are two timelines to work on. Search can reflect changes within weeks; training data changes only when new models ship.

1. **Make sure you can be found.** Check robots.txt and make sure you are not blocking OAI-SearchBot if you want to appear in ChatGPT search, and that your host or CDN allows OpenAI's published search-bot IP addresses. OpenAI notes that placement is still not guaranteed. Decide separately whether to allow GPTBot. Ensure key pages render without heavy client-side scripts and are indexable.
2. **State clear, consistent facts.** Publish plain pages that say what you do, who it is for, pricing, locations and how you compare to alternatives. Keep the same facts on your site, profiles, directories and review platforms, so whichever page gets retrieved tells the same story.
3. **Get cited by third parties.** Many answers lean on sources other than your own site. Earn inclusion in the comparison articles, review sites and community discussions that already appear in ChatGPT's citations for your category. Our guide to [getting your brand mentioned in ChatGPT](/blog/how-to-get-your-brand-mentioned-in-chatgpt) covers content and PR tactics.
4. **Answer the questions buyers ask.** Pages built around real questions ("best X for Y", "X vs Y", "how much does X cost") are easier for search to retrieve and quote. This is the core of [generative engine optimization](/generative-engine-optimization), and our [how to rank on ChatGPT](/how-to-rank-on-chatgpt) playbook goes step by step.
5. **Measure what ChatGPT actually says.** Run buyer-style prompts repeatedly and note which sources get cited. To understand how retrieval and ranking pick products, see [how AI search engines recommend products](/blog/how-ai-search-engines-recommend-products).

You can do this by hand with a spreadsheet, or use a tool such as AI Brand Track to speed up the measurement step. ## FAQ

### How does ChatGPT find its answers?

It generates answers from patterns learned during training, predicting text one token at a time. When search runs, it also rewrites your question into search queries, reads the retrieved pages and writes an answer with citations. It may also use your memory, custom instructions, uploaded files or connected apps.

### Does ChatGPT get information from the internet?

Yes. OpenAI says search tools are enabled for all models by default, and ChatGPT may search automatically when a question needs current information. You can tell search was used if the response shows web citations or a Sources panel. Without search, answers come from training data only.

### Does ChatGPT get its information from Google?

OpenAI doesn't say so. Its help center says ChatGPT search sometimes partners with other search providers and links to Microsoft's and Shopify's privacy policies. OpenAI also runs its own search crawler, OAI-SearchBot.

### Are ChatGPT citations real?

Citations from a web search link to real pages, but OpenAI warns they can be incomplete, outdated or incorrect, so open them and check. References given without search, such as a study title or quote with no link, can be fabricated. Always verify before you rely on them.

### Can GPT be trusted?

It can be useful, but OpenAI itself recommends treating it as a first draft and verifying important information. It can hallucinate facts and sound confident while wrong. Use search with citations and check the sources when accuracy matters.

### How does ChatGPT know so much about me?

Mostly from what you've shared. Depending on your settings, ChatGPT can use past chats, saved memories, custom instructions, files and connected apps such as Gmail. You can review and manage this under Settings, Personalization, Memory, or use an unpersonalized Temporary Chat.

### Is your data safe with ChatGPT?

OpenAI provides controls: you can turn off memory, delete saved memories and chats, opt out of model improvement and use Temporary Chat, which is not used to improve models while it stays temporary (OpenAI may still keep a copy for up to 30 days for safety purposes). Even so, avoid sharing passwords, financial details or sensitive personal data you wouldn't want stored.

### What questions does ChatGPT not answer?

It is trained to avoid requests for private or sensitive information about individuals and to decline harmful requests. It also can't reliably answer questions about events after its training cutoff unless it searches, or about pages it can't access because of paywalls or robots.txt.
